source: NCERT Class XI, Performing Arts & Cultural Heritage of India, Ch. 1 (Classical Dance Forms of India).

sections.heading: 1. Basis of Classical Dance
points: Indian classical dance is rooted in the **Natyashastra** of **Bharata Muni** (the foundational treatise on dance/drama).

Elements: **nritta** (pure dance/rhythm), **nritya** (expression + rhythm), **natya** (drama), and **abhinaya** (expression, esp. facial/**mudras/hastas** hand gestures) conveying **rasa** (emotion) and **bhava**.
The **Sangeet Natak Akademi** recognises **eight classical dance forms**.

sections.heading: 2. The Classical Dance Forms and Their States
points: **Bharatanatyam** — Tamil Nadu (temple/Devadasi tradition; fire-like poses).
**Kathak** — North India (UP; storytelling, spins/chakkars, Hindu + Mughal court influence).
**Kathakali** — Kerala (dance-drama, elaborate make-up/masks, male dancers, epics).
**Kuchipudi** — Andhra Pradesh (dance-drama, includes dancing on a brass plate — tarangam).
**Odissi** — Odisha (temple dance, tribhanga posture, Jagannath tradition).
**Manipuri** — Manipur (gentle, devotional, Raslila of Krishna).
**Mohiniyattam** — Kerala (graceful 'dance of the enchantress', lasya, women).
**Sattriya** — Assam (from Vaishnava monasteries/sattras, founded by Sankaradeva).

sections.heading: 3. Key Features and Patrons
points: Many forms began as **temple dances** (Bharatanatyam, Odissi) or **court dances** (Kathak).
Reformers/revivers: **Rukmini Devi Arundale** (Bharatanatyam revival), **Sankaradeva** (Sattriya).
**Mudras (hand gestures), footwork (tala/rhythm), and abhinaya** are common to all.

sections.heading: 4. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Natyashastra (Bharata Muni) = foundational text of dance/drama.
Eight classical dances: Bharatanatyam (TN), Kathak (UP/North), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (AP), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), Sattriya (Assam).
Kathakali = dance-drama with elaborate make-up; Kuchipudi = tarangam (brass plate).
Sattriya founded by Sankaradeva (Assam Vaishnava sattras).
Rukmini Devi Arundale revived Bharatanatyam.

sections.heading: 5. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Kathakali and Mohiniyattam are both from Kerala** (Kathakali = drama; Mohiniyattam = graceful lasya).
**Sattriya = Assam** (Sankaradeva); **Odissi = Odisha**.
**Kathak** is the only major North Indian classical dance (Hindu + Mughal court).
The **Natyashastra** by **Bharata Muni** is the source text.
